title: The Windows reds release CI found on the carried low batch
description: Release-tier CI run 40877191420 on the head that landed P148 failed on Windows only: case ww2 in tests/test_drive_phase.py on both Windows selftest legs (a case P148.1 added, never before run on Windows), and case sr9 in tests/test_stamp_verification.py on the Windows resample leg. Each task finds the cause on Windows rather than relaxing the case.
desiredOutcome: The release tier is green on every runner, Windows included, at the head 3.7.0 is cut from

findings.issue: On Windows, `confirmed` in _run_in now depends only on whether the root process has exited (`confirmed and proc.poll() is not None`). `_proc_group.drain` swallows its own TimeoutExpired and returns "". So a process outside the `taskkill /T` tree that still holds the output pipe (an orphan whose parent exited before the kill) survives the bounded drain, and the result still says 'was torn down' with no '(not confirmed)'. The docstring says the drain waits 'for every process holding its output pipe to let go', but whether that wait succeeded never reaches the confirmation. Nothing is misreported as removed: `_remove_throwaway`'s disk-and-list check is still the backstop that yields E_LEFT_BEHIND.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.3-hwg (b7386fe646fd): Have `_proc_group.drain` say whether it reached EOF (for example, return `(text, complete)`), and AND that result into `confirmed` in _run_in. `_proc_group.py` is not one of this task's declared files, so this needs a follow-up task. Until then, narrow the docstring to say the confirmation covers the root only.

findings.issue: No case covers `group=True` on _isolate's reset calls (`checkout -f`, `clean -ffdxq`), and none covers the new '(not confirmed)' wording when the root is still alive after the drain. Removing either change leaves the whole suite green. The executor's own outcome says so: 'Not covered by a case: the group=True on _isolate's reset calls, and the `(not confirmed)` wording.'
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.3-hwg (b7386fe646fd): Add a case where the build succeeds and the reset's `checkout -f` hangs in a smudge filter. Gate the filter on a marker file that the fixture creates after the build, so only the reset triggers it. Assert events == ['kill', 'drain', 'remove'] and could-not-prove. Add a second case that swaps tear_down to return True and drain to return "" with a root still alive, and assert the problem ends in '(not confirmed)'.

findings.issue: The _CLOCK_LITERALS_JUDGED entry says skb1's build 'is what times out on every runner, a slower one only sooner'. That does not hold. Under `--timeout 1`, several ungrouped git calls run before the build, each on the same one-second floor: leftover_throwaways, `rev-parse`, _at_head (stamp-verification.py:3619), head_tree and _cat_blobs. On a runner slow enough for one of them to overrun, red stops before the build and skb1 reads events == ['remove']. That is a red caused by load, not by the code: the same 'under resample load' exposure the task asked a fix not to depend on.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.3-hwg (b7386fe646fd): Give skb1 a deadline the pre-build reads can meet: the filter sleeps far past any small `--timeout`, so the build is still what times out. Alternatively, swap the pre-build reads for fixed answers in skb1. Then reword the judged reason to what holds.

findings.issue: Inherited test, read and not run. sr9 claims 'a run that times out ... is could-not-prove', but its timeout half never starts that run. The whole deadline is `--timeout 1`. The build is given `max(1, _left(deadline))` (stamp-verification.py:4131-4132). After the build, red sets 'building the throwaway spent the N-second deadline' whenever `_left(deadline) < 1` (:4133-4135), which always holds by then, and _isolated_run would refuse anyway (:3684). So `time.sleep(30)` is never spawned, and the 'timed out' sr9 asserts comes from the build or the spent deadline, never from _run_in's timeout teardown. sr9 would still pass if _run_in's TimeoutExpired arm were deleted. The ladder cases (_one_deadline_tries, _build_counted) are what reach that arm. This shape is also what made the task description read sr9 as a timed-out run.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.3-hwg (b7386fe646fd): Either retitle sr9's timeout half to what it reaches (a deadline spent before the run starts), or give it a deadline the build fits inside and assert the run's own basis, 'the run timed out after ... process group was torn down'. Add a red-first mutation to prove the case: remove the tear_down call in _run_in.

findings.issue: _ordinary_task_gate passes only tests.add paths to the slot fill, so a derived task gate leaves out a suite the task declares in its files (reported by P149.4's executor, outside its files)
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.7-hwg (70a9023efdb5): Derive the union of tests.add and declared suite files, each once

findings.issue: run-test-gate.py and drive-phase.py judge a timed-out run's teardown confirmed from the kill alone, without the drain-to-EOF check the red-first path now uses (reported by P149.3's executor, outside its files)
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.8-hwg (fdb54605265d): Use _proc_group.drain_to_eof in both readers

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'One helper, no second copy of the rule': the rule the task defines ('a teardown is reported confirmed only when the root exited and the drain reached EOF') is written out by hand as `confirmed = confirmed and complete and proc.poll() is not None` after a separate tear_down + drain_to_eof pair in each reader. Before the diff it lived once (stamp-verification _run_in); after it, three identical copies, so a fourth reader, or a change to the rule such as dropping the `poll()` term that `complete` already implies, has to be made three times. The executor reported this rather than fixing it, because the one place for it is plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_proc_group.py, which is outside the declared files. The task description is the half that cannot be met as written.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.9-hwg (844ba48fa589): Add one helper to _proc_group.py, e.g. `stop_and_drain(proc)` -> `(text, confirmed)`, which runs tear_down, drain_to_eof and the exited check. Replace the three-line block in _run_in, _shell and run_lint_probe with a call to it, and pin it in tests/test__proc_group.py in both directions (kill confirmed + drain incomplete -> False; both complete -> True). Run this as a follow-up task that declares _proc_group.py, its suite and the three readers. lc10e/lc10f and lp9b/lp9c then stub the helper's two inputs, as they do now.

findings.issue: Outside this diff's lines. Filed as a finding at the orchestrator's direction because it is why this task's red-first came back could-not-prove. The red-first helper's deadline split cannot fit this command, and its wording hides that. (a) sized_deadline and sweep_budget read the sweep's recorded slot-seconds as wall seconds. For this command they total 5109 (tests/test_drive_phase.py 4913.6 + tests/test_run_test_gate.py 194.7 in .github/sweep-costs.json). The deadline is capped at 565 and the fix-run reserve at 282, so `early` = 283 s is the whole window for BOTH the baseline and the task run. The recorded task gate for this exact command took durationMs 368645 (evidence row, runId 2026-10-29T15:05:34Z.70a002), so even one run does not fit in 283 s, and the three runs a proof needs cannot fit in 565 s. (b) Nothing reserves a share for the task run: the baseline spent about 276 s of the window, and _timed_run still started the task run because at least 1 s was left, giving it 7 s. (c) The basis then reads 'the run timed out after 7 s', which looks like the suite being slow, when the helper only gave it 7 s and knew before the first run that the proof could not fit. Every task whose gate sweeps tests/test_drive_phase.py hits the same could-not-prove, after about 283 s of wasted runs.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.10-hwg (1dc3ab5c9eeb): Before the first run, compare what the proof needs (baseline + task run + fix run, in wall terms, not summed slot-seconds) with the sized deadline. When it cannot fit, refuse at once with could-not-prove and name the shortfall (needed vs. allowed, and the figures behind each). Give the task run a held-back share as the fix run already has, so the baseline cannot spend it. When a run is started with less than its share, word the basis that way ('started with N s of the M s window after the baseline spent K s'). For a staged suite, size and run only the blocks that hold the task's new cases (the sweep's --stage) so the proof fits. Pin each case in tests/test_stamp_verification.py with a cost table whose total exceeds MAX_TIMEOUT.

findings.issue: The guide's sized_deadline paragraph still says the red-first deadline is the per-cost factor over the recorded slot-seconds; since P149.10 it is the factor over the wall time the proof's runs need, a proof that cannot fit is refused before any run, and the guide's _proc_group section does not name stop_and_drain, the one home of the teardown rule since P149.9 (reported by both executors, outside their files)
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.11-hwg (4aa21b1ba794): Restate both paragraphs from the code as it stands

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "No number written into prose": the new stop_and_drain paragraph writes cardinalities - "all three hold", "so the three cannot come to disagree", "this module's two functions", "Two callers still tear down without it". The last is the one that rots: it is true of the tree today (derive-phase-gate.py:202-203 and run-agent-session.py:444 are the only non-stop_and_drain teardowns) and goes false the day either migrates, while the names beside it stay right. The prose lint passes only because it does not know these shapes (a plain 'the N noun' is author-enforced, per CLAUDE.md).
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.12-hwg (69ab4da87549): Delete the numbers and keep the names: 'only when each of these holds: ...', 'so the callers cannot come to disagree', 'this module's tear_down and drain_to_eof', 'Callers that still tear down without it and record no confirmation: derive-phase-gate._spawn ..., run-agent-session.run_session ...'.

findings.issue: The line starts with "- and calls the teardown confirmed only when ..." (the dash is a sentence dash that wrapped to a line start). In CommonMark/GitHub a bullet can interrupt a paragraph, so the page renders the tail of the sentence as a list item and splits the paragraph.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.12-hwg (69ab4da87549): Re-wrap so the dash is not the first character of a line (e.g. put 'full pipe -' at the end of the previous line, as the paragraph above does with 'and').

findings.issue: "each wording an unconfirmed answer its own way" is not true of drive-phase.run_lint_probe: its docstring (drive-phase.py:8231-8233) says it takes the wording stamp-verification red gives, and its suffix " (not confirmed)" (drive-phase.py:8250-8251) is identical to stamp-verification._run_in's (stamp-verification.py:3350-3351). Only run-test-gate (facts["teardown"] = "unconfirmed", run-test-gate.py:3150-3151) words it differently. stop_and_drain's own docstring says the same 'its own way', so the guide copies a loose phrase.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.12-hwg (69ab4da87549): Say what is true: run-test-gate records teardown: unconfirmed in its facts, while stamp-verification._run_in and drive-phase.run_lint_probe append '(not confirmed)' to the timeout sentence.

findings.issue: The run list "HEAD's own, the task's, the second (--introduces) and the fix run" is presented as every run the one deadline covers, but red_run also makes a 'task-held' re-run (stamp-verification.py:4333-4344, guarded by start_problem(['task-held'], ...)) when inline-pulled-in code made the task's run green. The task asked that every sentence be true of the code; the enumeration is closed and omits that run.
findings.resolution: fixed in P149.12-hwg (69ab4da87549): Add the conditional re-run with the task's run held back to the list, or word it as 'every run red makes' without a closed enumeration.

findings.issue: Inherited-tests judgement from reading: the task's gate selects two lint suites that assert the guide's structure (path, enumeration, prose-number shapes), none of its claims. Both would still pass with the whole stop_and_drain paragraph and the rewritten deadline paragraph deleted or made false.
findings.resolution: Accept as inherent to a prose task, or file a task for a case that checks the guide's named functions (stop_and_drain, drain_to_eof, fit_problem, start_problem, sweep_budget) still exist in the code it names.
findings.acceptedReason: Both Windows reds the release CI found are fixed at their cause: ww2's fixture wrote text-mode CRLF (P149.1), and a timed-out throwaway build left a locked tree a single --force could not remove (P149.2). The review findings on that work are fixed: one teardown helper every reader calls (P149.3, .8, .9), a red-first deadline sized in wall time that refuses a proof that cannot fit (P149.10), derived gates that name each declared suite once (P149.4, .7), and a guide that states both (P149.11, .12). P149-R14 is left: it says the guide paragraphs' truth has no test, which no suite can hold; the per-task review is what checked it. Per-task reviewer answers continued over: P149.8-hwg intent diverges: Nastavi + fix task (Recommended)

tasks.title: A wave writer session's edit on Windows is filed from its member tree and leaves the project tree's file as the base held it
tasks.description: Release CI (run 40877191420, jobs 'selftests (windows, plain 4)' and 'selftests (windows, cp1252 4)') fails tests/test_drive_phase.py case ww2 deterministically on Windows; it passes on Linux and macOS. The case's own repr on Windows shows the filing succeeded (gate P1.2 green, work carried in refs/audit/carry/P1.2) and the carried blob is 'changed by P1.2\n'; the conjunct that fails is therefore one of: _filed_body(mpath, filer) is None, or the project tree's src/f2.txt is not b'v0\n' (on Windows it may hold the member's edit, or CRLF bytes from a checkout under core.autocrlf - read which). Find which conjunct fails and why on Windows - the case was added by P148.1 (d83aeee9) in _wave_writer_cases; the code paths are the drive's writer filing from a member tree in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py and the tree helpers in plugins/audit/scripts/git/_worktrees.py, and the test's helpers _play_session, _read, _filed_body. If the product writes or restores the project tree's file on Windows, fix the product; if the case reads bytes a Windows checkout legitimately rewrites (line endings), make the fixture deterministic (e.g. the fixture repo's own .gitattributes or core.autocrlf=false in _wave_repo) rather than loosening the assertion. You cannot run Windows here: reason from the code and the CI repr, state the cause with the line you read, and add or keep a case that would go red on Linux/macOS for the same defect where one can exist. Edit only the declared files; a fix that needs another file is reported, not made. No F/P/BUG ids in code, comments or docstrings. No number written into prose.

outcome.technical:
Cause: the fixture, not the product. tests/test_drive_phase.py _repo wrote every src/f<n>.txt with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') and fh.write('v0
') (base lines 147-150). Python text mode translates '
' to os.linesep on write, so on Windows the project tree's src/f2.txt held b'v0
' from the start, and ww2's last conjunct `_read(root/src/f2.txt) == b'v0
'` was false there with the product never touching the file. The sweep sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, so Git for Windows' system core.autocrlf is not read and no checkout is involved - the root file is the one the fixture wrote. The CI repr's other conjuncts were all visibly true (gate P1.2 green, carried blob 'changed by P1.2
', 'P1.2 writer return filed by the drive'). Reproduced locally: emulating the Windows bytes in _repo turned ww2 red (3/4 in sr2-block) with the CI's repr shape. Fix (tests/test_drive_phase.py only): _repo now writes its source files through the file's existing _write_lf helper (newline='
', utf-8), with a comment stating the constraint; ww2's assertion is unchanged in strictness (still the literal b'v0
'), and its repr now carries every conjunct's value (filed, filed_said, carried, the project file's bytes) so a future red names its conjunct. drive-phase.py and _worktrees.py unchanged. Runs: `python3 tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage sr2-block` exit 0, 4/4, ww2 repr ends ', 'changed by P1.2
', b'v0
')'; `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py` exit 0, '1/1 files ok, 671 cases' (run although the brief said own-tests had nothing to run - stated rather than hidden); `ruff check tests/test_drive_phase.py` exit 0; `vermin -t=3.8- --no-tips --violations tests/test_drive_phase.py` exit 0. A Linux/macOS case for the same defect cannot exist (text-mode translation is a Windows property); ww2's byte conjunct stays the case that goes red on any OS if the product writes the member's edit into the project tree. Class sweep: grep '"v0\n"' in the file - other text-mode writers at extra_files (~6098), _wave_repo spare f3 (~7487), notes.txt fixtures (~11278, ~11297) left, because no case compares their bytes against a literal; the other byte-literal assertions in the file (e.g. 1786, 7986, 8397, 8436, 8676, 9292) were green on Windows in the CI log (only ww2 FAILed in that shard). Dependants: tests/test_drive_phase.py - still correct for every listed dependant: no case id, stage label or helper name changed (_counting, _follower_cases, _git_said, _head untouched), so sweep-costs.json blocks, ci.yml, affected.py, sweep-selftests.py, test__runner_output.py, test_run_test_gate.py and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md read the same file shape; fixture bytes change only on Windows (LF instead of CRLF), and on POSIX they are identical. drive-phase.py and _worktrees.py: not edited, so all their dependants are unaffected.
outcome.descriptive: ww2's Windows red was the fixture writing CRLF via text mode; _repo now writes LF bytes and ww2's repr names every conjunct.

redFirst.basis: regression task with tests.add none and expectRedFirst false: no case of its own to prove through the helper, and the defect is Windows-only (text-mode newline translation), so a HEAD-vs-fix run on this macOS host is green on both sides. The cause was reproduced before the fix instead, by hand in the task tree: _repo's source-file write temporarily given newline='\r\n' (the bytes Windows text mode writes) -> `python3 tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage sr2-block` exit 1, 'FAIL ww2 ... gate P1.2 green; work of P1.2 carried ...', 'SELFTEST FAILED: 3/4 cases passed' - the same shape as the CI repr; file restored from a byte copy before the fix was written (git diff --stat empty).
redFirst.at: 2026-10-29, before the fix, in the task's own worktree

tasks.title: A red-first run that times out on Windows removes its throwaway instead of reporting it left behind
tasks.description: Release CI (run 40877191420, job 'resample (windows)') fails tests/test_stamp_verification.py case sr9: the timeout half returned exit 4 (E_LEFT_BEHIND, stamp-verification.py) with no redFirst block, where could-not-prove (3) with the throwaway removed is required; the cannot-start half passed. The test runs `python -c 'import time; time.sleep(30)'` under --timeout 1 in a throwaway tree. On Windows a killed child (or its grandchild, if the command runs through a shell or launcher) can still hold the throwaway directory or a file in it open when removal runs, so the removal fails. Find the code path in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py that kills a timed-out red run and removes the throwaway: make the kill reach the whole process tree on Windows and wait for it to exit (bounded) before removal, and/or retry removal on Windows sharing errors within a bound; keep E_LEFT_BEHIND for a removal that really cannot be done. Under resample load this is intermittent, so the fix must not depend on timing luck; a case that pins the ordering (kill, wait, then remove) on any platform is preferred over a sleep. You cannot run Windows here: reason from the code, state the cause with the line you read. Edit only the declared files; a fix that needs another file is reported, not made. No F/P/BUG ids in code, comments or docstrings. No number written into prose.

outcome.technical:
CAUSE (read from HEAD's code, reproduced on macOS): sr9 runs with --timeout 1, and red's build of the throwaway gets `max(1, _left(deadline))` (run_red -> _build_throwaway). On a loaded runner it is that `git worktree add` which times out, not the sleeping run. HEAD's _git (stamp-verification.py, `subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout)`) kills only the direct git child; the git process `worktree add` starts to check the tree out (and any filter it starts) keeps running inside the throwaway, and on Windows `subprocess.run` then communicate()s with no bound. The killed add also leaves its 'initializing' lock, and HEAD's _remove_throwaway asked `git worktree remove --force` once, which git refuses for a locked tree, so the tree stayed listed: exit 4 (E_LEFT_BEHIND), with the ERROR line on stderr appended to the JSON so the suite's _red parsed nothing - exactly sr9's Windows tuple (4, None, None). Reproduced here: a probe killing `git worktree add` part way then calling HEAD's _remove_throwaway left 27 of 30 throwaways behind (`git worktree remove --force` -> exit 128 'cannot remove a locked working tree, lock reason: initializing'); the HEAD-code run of skb1 printed exit=4 events=['remove'] listed=True, and the survivor found afterwards (pid 31070, `python -c import time; time.sleep(120)`) had its cwd inside /var/folders/.../audit-red-jd1_y92z/tree; I stopped it. The timed-out RUN path (_run_in) already tore down its process group and drained it, so it is not where sr9 failed. Windows not run: the cause on Windows is inferred from the same code path plus the matching exit/shape, not observed.
CHANGES, plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py: (1) _git(..., group=False) gains `group=True`, which runs the call through _run_in - a process group (_proc_group.group_kwargs), torn down whole on a timeout (_proc_group.tear_down: killpg on POSIX, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows) and drained (_proc_group.drain, bounded by GRACE_SECONDS) before returning; used by the calls that WRITE the throwaway: _build_throwaway's `worktree add` and _isolate's `checkout -f` / `clean`. (2) _remove_throwaway asks `git worktree remove --force --force` (one --force does not remove a locked worktree; the path is the run's own throwaway). Removal still runs once, in red's finally, after _run_in returned - so the order is kill, drain/wait, then remove. (3) _run_in: after tear_down and drain, `confirmed = confirmed and proc.poll() is not None`, so on Windows (where taskkill returning 0 only means the kill was asked for) a root still running after the bounded drain is said as `(not confirmed)`; docstring states the ordering. (4) The deadline-budget comment above REMOVE_GIT_TIMEOUT now says the one teardown it budgets may be a build/reset git call's; TEARDOWN_MARGIN and the removal's two git calls are unchanged. Left on purpose: a registration whose directory exists without its `.git` file (add killed between those two writes) is still refused by git and reported left behind (docstring says so); no ENOTEMPTY retry was added to the shared while_shared (that is _output.py, not declared).
tests/test_stamp_verification.py: new block `sr-killed-build` (_killed_build_cases) in STAGES: skb1 drives red with --timeout 1 on a fixture whose HEAD carries a file under a smudge filter that sleeps, so the build is what times out on any runner; tear_down/drain/_remove_throwaway are swapped for recorders that call through, and the case asserts exit 3, status could-not-prove, 'timed out' in the basis, events == ['kill', 'drain', 'remove'] exactly, removed True, path gone, and no throwaway in `git worktree list`. skb2 locks a throwaway with reason 'initializing' and asserts _remove_throwaway removes it from disk and list. `--timeout 1` judged in _CLOCK_LITERALS_JUDGED for _killed_build_cases (sk1 green); sr162's _git fake widened to accept `group`.
RUNS (development checks, not gates; the brief names nothing of the task's own to run): `python3 tests/test_stamp_verification.py --selftest --stage sr-killed-build` -> ALL PASS 2/2, exit 0, run four times with 5 s gaps; blocks sr-located 14/14, sr-red 15/15 (sr9 included), sr-remove-retry 7/7, sr-listing 3/3, sr-crlf 1/1, sr-every-run-isolated 9/9, sr-budget 9/9 (sk1, sk2, sr42), all exit 0; ruff check on both files: All checks passed; vermin -t=3.8-: no violations; _output_lints.prose_number_claims('.') and house_style_violations(): no hit in either file. Mutations, each in a scratch worktree at HEAD with my two files copied in (never in my tree): build call without group=True -> skb1 FAIL (0/1 at the time); single --force -> skb2 FAIL, skb1 PASS (POSIX kill is SIGTERM, which git answers by removing the tree it was building, lock included - so skb1 meets the lock only on Windows, which is why skb2 exists); restored copy -> 2/2. Not covered by a case: the group=True on _isolate's reset calls, and the `(not confirmed)` wording.
DEPENDANTS: tools/affected.py - names the file by path; still correct, no path moved. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md - says TEARDOWN_MARGIN is one teardown plus the removal's two git calls; still true (the removal still makes two git calls; the teardown may now be a build git call's). audit-plan.schema.json - redFirst enum untouched. _output.py - while_shared/SHARING_WAIT_SECONDS used as before. _proc_group.py - group_kwargs/tear_down/drain used unchanged, now also for two git calls. _runner_output.py - untouched. drive-phase.py - calls red as a command; exit codes and payload keys unchanged. run-test-gate.py - basename mention only; unaffected. tests/test__filed_returns.py (_crlf_cases) and tools/affected.py (_scan) - untouched. .github/sweep-costs.json - no figure for the new block sr-killed-build; the sweep weighs it by the suite's figure over its blocks; re-recording costs is the orchestrator's call. tools/sweep-selftests.py, tools/verify.sh - name the file only; unchanged.
outcome.descriptive: A red-first build of the throwaway that times out now has its whole git process tree killed and drained before removal, and the removal gets past the lock a killed `git worktree add` leaves, so it is could-not-prove with the throwaway removed rather than exit 4

tasks.title: The red-first helper sizes its runs in wall time and refuses up front a proof that cannot fit, instead of timing out a run it never gave time
tasks.description: Fix review finding P149-R8 (docs/audit/phases/P149.json review.findings): the red-first helper in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py sizes its deadline from the recorded sweep cost in slot-seconds (sized_deadline, sweep_budget) and reads it as wall-clock seconds, then caps the whole proof at the host's limit and holds half back for the fix run, so a suite whose single recorded gate run takes longer than the window left (tests/test_drive_phase.py: a recorded run of about six minutes) gets the baseline run and then a task run started with seconds left, and the basis says 'the run timed out after N s' when the helper gave it N s. Every task whose gate sweeps a long suite comes back could-not-prove this way. Fix: convert recorded slot-seconds to the wall time the sweep will actually take (the sweep runs blocks in parallel - read how tools/sweep-selftests.py schedules them and use the same reading, or measure from the recorded gate run's wall time when the plan has one), and when the runs the proof needs cannot fit the deadline, say so BEFORE starting them - could-not-prove with a basis naming the measured need and the deadline - rather than starting a run that cannot finish and reporting its timeout as the cause. A task run started with less time than its measured need is never reported as having timed out on its own. Cases in tests/test_stamp_verification.py, each proven red first: slot-seconds are not read as wall seconds; a proof that cannot fit is refused up front with that basis; a proof that fits is unchanged. No case may rest on a short deadline surviving a loaded runner - drive the arithmetic through recorded costs and a fake clock, not a real sleep.
